narration.text: Is GPT better than Opus? That depends on what you measure. The strongest case is not that one model wins every task. It is where GPT gets you more for each dollar.

Start with listed API prices. GPT-6.1 Sol lists at two dollars per million input tokens and ten dollars per million output. Opus 5.5 lists at four and twenty. That is half the standard token price on both sides, but not half the cost of every completed job.

On AutomationBench, OpenAI reports GPT-6.1 Sol beating Opus 5.5 by 2.2 percentage points at medium reasoning, at roughly one-third the task cost. This is a vendor-reported comparison, not a universal score.

For a science-workflow evaluation, OpenAI reports average task costs of five dollars and forty-seven cents for GPT-6.1 Sol, versus twenty-three dollars and twenty-one cents for Opus 5.5 at maximum effort. Cost is only one part of the result.
And Opus has wins too. Anthropic reports Opus 5.5 at 66.4 percent on Terminal-Bench 4.0, versus 57.9 for GPT-6 Astra. Different effort settings matter, but this alone rejects a blanket winner claim.
The fair conclusion: GPT-6.1 Sol's edge is price and cost efficiency on selected workflows. Opus remains formidable at coding. Test both on your tasks, tracking quality, time, and total cost.
